confirmed.title: Combined chip counts print "1 engineers", "1 senior leaders" on the sample files
confirmed.what: While a chip is pressed, every other chip is relabelled `${count} ${s.short}`, and `short` is always the plural. On the shipped samples this gives wrong grammar the first time a user combines two chips. On a five-person file the plain label is already wrong: "1 senior leaders" (insights.js:135 builds every label from a fixed plural `short`).
confirmed.evidence: countIfAdded on the samples, rendered the way Chip renders it. Founder file: press "44 founders and CEOs" and the Microsoft chip reads "1 at Microsoft"; press "19 at Microsoft" and the other reads "1 founders and CEOs". Healthcare: "22 at Massachusetts General Hospital" then "1 operations people". Small: "7 connected…" then "1 investors". Five-person LinkedIn file: shortcuts include "1 senior leaders".
confirmed.fix: Store `one` and `many` forms on each Shortcut (the role family's one/many, "senior leader", "person tagged"…). Choose the form by count in both make() and Chip.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced on the five-person file: plain chip "1 senior leaders" (insights.js:194, fixed plural). Chip:14 uses the plural `short` for role chips, so a combined count of 1 reads "1 founders and CEOs". Overstated in part: "1 at Microsoft", "1 tagged…" and "1 connected…" are correct English. Only role and senior chips are wrong. This is a grammar slip, not misleading.

confirmed.title: Place and company sentences claim a lead that is really a tie
confirmed.what: When several cities or companies tie for first, the alphabetically first one is presented as the leader. "More are in France (80) than anywhere else" is false when five countries each hold 80. The company sentence has the same tie problem.
confirmed.evidence: Conference list (400 people, 80 each in USA/UK/Germany/India/France): "More are in France (80) than anywhere else." No-company file (24 in each of 5 cities): "More are in Austin (24) than anywhere else." All-investors file (5 firms × 18): "The most at Accel (18), then Benchmark (18)." 3,000 file: "The most at Acme Corp (273) and Contoso (273)."
confirmed.fix: When cities[1][1] === cities[0][1], say "Spread evenly: 80 each in France, Germany…" or drop the sentence. Likewise for companies: say "18 each at…" instead of "the most… then".
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced. A 400-person conference file with 80 people in each of 5 countries reads "More are in France (80) than anywhere else." The investor file reads "The most at Accel (18), then Benchmark (18)." The city sentence is false when there is a tie (line 283). The company sentence is only misleading. Exact ties at the top are rare in real files, so this is minor.

confirmed.title: Tag-led files never show a role or industry chip, even under More
confirmed.what: More is filled in plan order with every remaining chip of the earlier types, so it reaches the 12-chip cap before role or industry is considered. On the sales CRM there is no role chip anywhere, yet one of the example questions is "Which sales and marketing people do I know?". On the fundraising list, the split between VC funds and allocators (25 in Venture capital) is missing, while 3- and 4-person company chips take its place.
confirmed.evidence: sales-crm: shortcuts = 3 tags, 2 companies, New York; more = "62 tagged decision maker", "57 champion", "45 churned", "14 at Greenfield Grocers", "12 at Northgate Pharmacy Group", "58 in Toronto". "102 sales and marketing people", "74 clinicians" and "80 in Healthcare" are absent. lp list: more ends with "4 at Yale Investments Office", "3 at Alder Capital"; Venture capital (25) is absent.
confirmed.fix: Fill More in two passes as well. First pass: the first unused chip of each type in plan order, role and industry included. Second pass: extra chips of the same types, until the cap.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced on sales-crm. More holds 3 tag, 2 company and 1 place chip and no role chip, yet the example question is "Which sales and marketing people do I know?" (102). On the LP list, More ends with "3 at Alder Capital". The loop at lines 229-235 drains each pool in plan order until it hits MAX_CHIPS.

confirmed.title: The industry chip repeats a company or role chip already on screen
confirmed.what: The industry pool has no overlap check, so the first six chips often hold two chips that light the same people. On the small sample, "7 in Software" is essentially Bluebird Labs plus one other person. That wastes one of six slots on a file that has few to spare.
confirmed.evidence: Jaccard overlap between chips shown together. Small sample: "6 at Bluebird Labs" vs "7 in Software" share 6 people (J=0.86). No-titles file: "23 at Stripe" and "23 in Fintech" (J=1.00). Five-person file: "3 at Stripe" and "3 in Fintech" (J=1.00). Conference: "50 senior leaders" and "50 founders and CEOs" (J=1.00). No-company: "12 in Software" and "12 engineers" (J=1.00).
confirmed.fix: In take(), skip a candidate whose keys overlap 80% or more with a chip already shown, and let the next candidate have the slot.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced. Five-person file: "3 at Stripe" and "3 in Fintech". File with no company column: "24 engineers" and "24 in Software". Healthcare: "58 in Education" shown next to "64 researchers and academics". take() (217-221) checks only the id and the Venture-capital special case, with no overlap test.

confirmed.title: Sectors built from job titles: "Strongest in Software (1,909)", students as "Education"
confirmed.what: When the employer is unknown, sector words in the job title decide the industry. Every "Software Engineer" counts as working in the Software sector, and every "Student" in the Education sector. As a result the read-out names a sector the user does not work in. The "in Software" and "in Education" chips then duplicate the engineers and students families.
confirmed.evidence: 3,000 engineers at Acme Corp, Contoso, Initech and so on: "Strongest in Software (1,909)." Conference list: "Strongest in Education (50)" and chip "50 in Education", all "Student @ Company N". One-company file (all Acme Corp): "Strongest in Software (20)" = the 20 Software Engineers.
confirmed.fix: Use only the company name for isSector labels: steps 1, 3 (on the company text) and 4. In profileNetwork, do not count a sector that came from the title alone.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced. 3,000 Software Engineers at 11 companies reads "Strongest in Software (3,000)." On the conference file the 50 people titled "Student" become the first-six chip "50 in Education", and "50 students and early-career people" sits under More. In grouping.js, line 172 (TITLE_INDUSTRY) and line 174 (sector words in the title) turn title words into a sector.

confirmed.title: Free-text notes become the lead chips and the default arrangement
confirmed.what: The parser pushes a Notes column into tags (parseContacts.js:388). tagProfile treats repeated notes as signal, so the read-out, the first three chips and the default "By tag" arrangement are built from the user's own jotted notes.
confirmed.evidence: A 100-person CSV with Name, Company, Title, Notes. Sentences: "By tag: 17 coffee next month, 17 intro via Jo, 17 met at SaaStr." Chips: "17 tagged “coffee next month”", "17 tagged “intro via Jo”", "17 tagged “met at SaaStr, follow up re: pilot”" (More also has "17 tagged “met at SaaStr”"). defaultGrouping = 'tag'.
confirmed.fix: Keep notes out of tags (a separate notes field), or exclude from tagProfile.useful any tag longer than about 3 words or containing punctuation.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced exactly. parseContacts.js:387-388 pushes the Notes cell into tags. Result: "By tag: 17 coffee next month, 17 intro via Jo, 17 met at SaaStr.", the chips "17 tagged “met at SaaStr, follow up re: pilot”" and "17 tagged “met at SaaStr”" both in the first six, and the default arrangement set to tag.

confirmed.title: An example question built from the file returns nobody (non-Latin city)
confirmed.what: The place question is offered with a count, but the rule parser does not read a non-Latin city. The engine answers 0 and shows the generic hint. The spec requires every example to return at least one person.
confirmed.evidence: A 60-person file with locations "Москва, Россия", "東京, 日本", "서울, 대한민국". Questions include "Who do I know in Москва?" (count 20). answerQuestion(useLlm false) gives filters.locations [], total 0, note "Ask about a company, a role, an industry or a place…". Company questions in Cyrillic and Hangul do work (15).

confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced. A 60-person file with "Москва, Россия" locations is offered "Who do I know in Москва?" (20). answerQuestion with useLlm false returns locations [], total 0. This breaks SPEC.md:224 (every example returns at least one person). The Latin-script company questions work (Sony 15, Toyota 15).

confirmed.title: An address book with only names and emails gets a card that says only what is missing
confirmed.what: For a personal address book the whole first screen is one sentence about what is missing: no chips, no example questions, no arrangement. Work email domains are a clear grouping signal in exactly this kind of file, and they are ignored.
confirmed.evidence: 250 contacts with Name and Email, 100 of them @stripe.com or @acme.com. Sentences: ["250 people. Most have no company or title in this file, so they cannot be grouped by employer or role."]; shortcuts []; more []; questions []; groupings []. The spec asks for "plus whatever facet does carry signal".
confirmed.fix: When company fill is under 50%, derive a company from non-webmail email domains (stripe.com becomes Stripe) for company chips and the sentence, labelled "from email addresses".
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: 250 contacts with name and email (100 at stripe.com or acme.com). The card is one sentence about what is missing, with no shortcuts, no More, no questions and no arrangements. SPEC.md:81 promises "plus whatever facet does carry signal", and nothing is computed from email.

confirmed.title: A recruiter's candidate list loads zero people; a Stage or Status column is ignored
confirmed.what: HEADER_MAP has no "candidate name" or "current company", so an ATS export yields no contacts at all. With plain headers, the "Stage" or "Status" column, the pipeline signal the spec builds tag chips on, is not mapped to tags. This code predates the change, but it decides the first thirty seconds for pipeline files.
confirmed.evidence: parseGenericCsv with headers [Candidate Name, Current Company, …] returns contacts [], headerFound false. With Name, Company, Title, Location, Status, Date Added: tags [] for everyone. Read-out: "You know 180 people at 12 companies: 180 engineers." and "180 connected in the last 12 months."; no stage chips.

Pre-existing in parseContacts.js HEADER_MAP (361-362), not new in this change, but it decides what a pipeline file shows.

confirmed.title: Industry and senior chips have no minimum size, so tiny files get chips of one or two people
confirmed.what: Tag, role and company chips require at least 3 people. Industry and senior chips have no such minimum, so small files get chips for a handful of people that add nothing.
confirmed.evidence: Five-person LinkedIn file (3 at Stripe, 2 at Google). Shortcuts: "4 engineers", "3 at Stripe", "3 in Fintech", "1 senior leaders", "2 in Big Tech". The Google company chip is rightly hidden (2 people), but "2 in Big Tech" is the same two people.
confirmed.fix: Add count >= 3 to the industry filter (line 165) and the senior filter (line 195).
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced on the five-person file: shortcuts "1 senior leaders" and "2 in Big Tech". The industry filter (165) and senior filter (195) use only share bounds and have no 3-person floor.

confirmed.title: Read-out states recency facts that cover everyone
confirmed.what: The recency sentence uses recentPool, which is not passed through fits(), so it can describe the whole file. The chip for the same window is rightly dropped.
confirmed.evidence: All-investors file (all connected 05 Nov 2025): "90 connected in the 12 months before this export." with n=90. Recruiter file: "180 connected in the last 12 months." with n=180.
confirmed.fix: Emit the sentence only when recentPool[0].count < n, or read "All connected in…".
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed by reading: line 285 uses recentPool[0] (pushed at 189 when count >= 5), never passed through fits(). When every dated person falls in the window, the sentence states "N connected…" with N = n, while the chip is dropped by fits().

confirmed.title: "The most at" sentence names 2-person companies or the only company
confirmed.what: topCompanies needs only 2 people, so a broad list reads "The most at Company 0 (2)", which tells the user nothing. A single-employer file reads "The most at Acme Corp (200)."
confirmed.evidence: Conference (400 people, 300 companies): "The most at Company 0 (2) and Company 1 (2)." One-company file: "You know 200 people at 1 company: …" then "The most at Acme Corp (200)."
confirmed.fix: Require the company-chip threshold (3 people and 2% of N). When C === 1, say "All at {company}" once, in the first sentence.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced on the conference file (300 companies): "The most at Company 0 (2) and Company 1 (2)." topCompanies (245) needs only 2 people per company.

confirmed.title: Company pool cut to four before choosing, so equal firms disappear while slots stay empty
confirmed.what: companyPool is sliced to 4 before chips are chosen. A file whose value is the firms gets 4 chips, two empty slots and no More, and an equal-sized firm is missing.
confirmed.evidence: 90 investors, 18 each at Sequoia Capital, Accel, Benchmark, Index Ventures and Greylock Partners. Shortcuts: "18 at Accel", "18 at Benchmark", "18 at Greylock Partners", "18 at Index Ventures"; more []. Sequoia Capital (18) is not offered.
confirmed.fix: Keep the full eligible company list (up to MAX_CHIPS) in the pool; the plan quotas already limit what shows first.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced. 90 investors split evenly over 5 firms get 4 company chips, More [] and no Sequoia Capital. The 3,000 file with 11 equal companies also gets only 4 chips and empty slots. companyPool is cut to 4 at line 160.

confirmed.title: Sparse read-out says "Most have no company" when nobody has one
confirmed.what: The sparse branch always says "Most", even when the column does not exist at all.
confirmed.evidence: A 120-person CSV with Name, Title, Location and no company column (fields.company = 0): "120 people. Most have no company in this file, so they cannot be grouped by employer."
confirmed.fix: Use "None have a company" when share('company') === 0, and "Most" otherwise.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced on a 120-person file with no company column: "120 people. Most have no company in this file…" Line 253 always says "Most".

confirmed.title: Second family in the read-out is an arbitrary pick among tied families
confirmed.what: familyRanked breaks ties alphabetically by key, so the read-out names "clinicians" as the second-largest group when eight families tie. A clinicians chip also takes a first-six slot.
confirmed.evidence: No-company file: families product 24, then engineers, sales, partners, people, data, clinicians, founders, others at 12 each. Read-out: "By title: 24 product and design people and 12 clinicians." Chips: "12 clinicians" in the first six, "12 engineers" under More.
confirmed.fix: When the next families tie, either list none after the leader or say "and several groups of 12".
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced on the file with no company column. Five families tie at 24, and the read-out says "By title: 24 clinicians and 24 engineers." The alphabetical tie-break at line 152 decides which two are named.

confirmed.title: Many files get fewer than three example questions
confirmed.what: The only fallback for a missing slot is a second company. Files with no company chip, or with no role chip, show two or zero examples even when other answerable forms exist (a second city, a second role).
confirmed.evidence: Questions shown: conference 2 (sales/marketing, France; Germany and engineers unused), one-company 2, no-company 2, 3,000-engineer 2, all-investors 2, duplicates 2, one-person 0.
confirmed.fix: Fill remaining slots from the second role chip and the second place chip, each checked to return at least one person.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: two questions each on the conference, investor, notes, no-company, 3,000-engineer and five-person files. Germany and India place chips go unused on the conference file. Lines 306-313 fall back only to a second company.

confirmed.title: At three active chips every other chip goes disabled with no reason and leaves the tab order
confirmed.what: `full` disables every inactive chip, More included, when three are pressed. A native disabled button cannot be focused and carries no title or text, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot find the remaining chips. Sighted users see them greyed with no explanation. The same applies to zero-result chips.
confirmed.evidence: disabled={!active && ((count != null && count === 0) || full)} on a plain <button>, with no title, aria-describedby or visible note.
confirmed.fix: Use aria-disabled (still focusable) with a short visible hint such as "Up to 3 at once" or "No one left", and keep the click as a no-op.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed at Shortcuts.js:44. A native `disabled` button with no title or hint is skipped in tab order, and nothing on screen explains the cap of three. A standard pattern, but there is no explanation, so it stays minor.

confirmed.title: Inactive chips silently change their number when another chip is pressed
confirmed.what: "22 at Stripe" becomes "3 at Stripe" after "investors" is pressed, with nothing to mark it as the count if added. A first-time user reads it as a fact about Stripe, and the combine behaviour is not explained anywhere on the card.
confirmed.evidence: label = active || count == null ? s.label : `${fmt(count)} ${s.short}`; no prefix, tooltip or helper text in Shortcuts.js or AtAGlance.js.
confirmed.fix: Show the intersection count as "+ 3 at Stripe" (or "3 of 22 at Stripe"), and add one muted line under the chips: "Press several to narrow".
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed at Shortcuts.js:14. Reproduced: with "201 engineers" pressed, "41 at Google" reads "22 at Google". There is no marker and no helper text in Shortcuts.js or AtAGlance.js. The comment at Shortcuts.js:3-5 describes the behaviour, but users never see it.

confirmed.title: Hiding every source leaves an empty read-out and "Everyone 0"
confirmed.what: The card renders when contacts.length > 0, but the profile is built from visibleContacts. Turning off every source chip gives an empty paragraph, the chip "Everyone 0" and no sentence saying why.
confirmed.evidence: hasContacts = contacts.length > 0 (line 212); profile = profileNetwork(visibleContacts) (line 502); for n === 0, sentences stays [] (insights.js:248) and everyone.label is "Everyone 0".
confirmed.fix: When visibleContacts is empty but contacts is not, show "All sources are hidden. Turn one back on to see your network." in place of the read-out.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed. network.js:212 sets hasContacts from contacts, while :502 profiles visibleContacts. The source toggle at :839 flips any source with no guard on the last one. With every source off, n=0, sentences=[] (insights.js:248) and the chip reads "Everyone 0".

confirmed.title: By company: every named company sits on the back of the globe, Other companies faces the viewer
confirmed.what: wrapOntoGlobe puts the largest top cluster at [0,0,1] and sends the next ones to whichever spot has the most room, which is the far side. Under By company the largest cluster is now the new 'Other companies' group (70% of people), so the first By company screen shows one 'Other companies' banner. Stripe, Google and the other named hubs sit behind it, faint and unlabelled, because company labels need q.z >= 0.2 (line 743).
confirmed.evidence: Jest on the fixtures, By company, centre z < 0 for: VC 544, 13 of 16 named (Stripe 22, Google 19, Goldman 12 ... Anthropic 6) behind 'Other companies 384'. Founder 451: 13 of 16 behind 'Other companies 267'. Sales CRM: Marlowe 18 and 11 more behind 'Other 207'. Healthcare: MGH 22 and 11 more behind. LP list: 12 behind. Should be the named companies in view.
confirmed.fix: In wrapOntoGlobe, keep the OTHER_COMPANIES_KEY node out of slot 0 (sort it last, or place it after the named hubs). Or place the first few named hubs on the front hemisphere next to the largest one, not at its antipode.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced with buildAtlas(...,{groupBy:'company'}) and wrapOntoGlobe. VC: '[OTHER] Other companies 384' z=1.00, Stripe 22 z=-1.00, Google z=-0.43, 13 of 16 named hubs z<0. Founder: Other 267 z=1, Google 41 z=-1. Sales: Other 207 z=1, Marlowe 18 z=-1. The Other group is new in atlas.js, so this is a regression from this change.
confirmed.betterFix: Sort the OTHER_COMPANIES_KEY node last before placeClusters. Also fix the root cause (globe-16): limit the first few greedy placements to the front hemisphere. Otherwise the second-largest named hub (Stripe) still lands at the antipode.

confirmed.title: Clicking a group no longer opens it; the camera barely moves and the breadcrumb stays at All
confirmed.what: Before the change, clicking a group or company called goTo, which ran cameraFor with least = 1.75 or 2.4 times home zoom. That opened the layer inside, and arrive told the page where you were. Now a click only lights the people, and the camera fits their 90% angle, about 1.1 times home zoom. That is below the sub-group threshold (1.2) and the company threshold (1.75), so nothing opens. flyTo is called without arrive, and reportView needs the group to fill 62% of the stage, so onViewNode and the breadcrumb stay at the root. The spec does not remove this drill-in.
confirmed.evidence: VC By role, Founders & executives (203): share 0.082, so angle 0.58 and s = 246/(1.5*(0.549+0.03)) = 283, against home 254 (zoom 1.11). showSub = clamp((1.11-1.2)/0.4) = 0 and showCompanies = 0. HEAD network.js:718-726 called goTo(node.id) for group and company clicks. The build report confirms the flight was removed.
confirmed.fix: For a group or company click, have the highlight turn use cameraFor(node) with arrive = node.id, or keep goTo in onNodeClick and skip the spread turn when selection.nodeId is set.
confirmed.verifierNote: HEAD network.js onNodeClick called goTo(node.id) for groups and companies (cameraFor with least 1.75/2.4). The new onNodeClick only calls setPick. The turn uses spreadOf: Founders 203 share 0.082, angle 0.58, a near-home zoom with no arrive, so reportView/breadcrumb stay at root. The build report confirms the flight was removed. SPEC section 3 keeps the breadcrumb and does not remove drill-in.

confirmed.title: After 'Arrange by' with a selection lit, the camera ignores the lit people
confirmed.what: The turn-to-selection effect depends only on [highlightIds]. Arrange by changes the atlas, but chip and company selections keep the same key Set, because profile depends only on visibleContacts. So the atlas effect flies home and nothing turns to the lit people. With Stripe selected, switching to By company leaves Stripe lit on the back of the globe (globe-1), with 'Other companies' in front. The '22 lit' count still shows. Full screen (a new size, fitNode(...,0)) also drops the turn.
confirmed.evidence: useEffect(() => { ... spreadOf(lit) ... flyTo(...) }, [highlightIds]); the atlas effect (lines 1035-1060) calls fitNode(root) on a new atlas. In page arrange(), pick keeps its keys and only nodeId becomes null. Combined with globe-1, Stripe has z<0 under By company.
confirmed.fix: Add atlas, globe and width/height to the turn effect's deps, and have it run after the atlas effect when a selection is active (skip the fitNode in that case).
confirmed.verifierNote: Turn effect deps are [highlightIds] only (line 1081). arrange() does setPick({...p,nodeId:null}), so keys keep the same Set, and goTo(ROOT_ID) flies home. Profile is memoised on visibleContacts only, so chip Sets survive too. Combined with globe-1, Stripe stays lit on the back under By company.

confirmed.title: The draw loop never stops while anything is selected, even off screen
confirmed.what: The loop requests the next frame whenever tr.size > 0, which is true whenever selectedId is set (the dashed trail animation). The page now passes selection.nodeId for every globe click on a group, company or person, so any click on the globe starts a full-scene redraw at display rate until the selection is cleared. It keeps running when the map is scrolled away (phone: panel first, globe below). It ignores reduced motion. A background click clears only openId, not the selection.
confirmed.evidence: jsdom, stub canvas, 30,000 generated people: after rerender with selectedId = a top group, 300 frames were run and a frame was still queued. Each frame averaged 11.3 ms with no rasterising. network.js:882 selectedId={openId || selection?.nodeId}. HEAD passed only person and company ids.
confirmed.fix: Animate the trail only while the canvas is intersecting (IntersectionObserver) and not under prefers-reduced-motion. Otherwise draw the trail static and stop the loop.
confirmed.verifierNote: Mostly pre-existing: HEAD already looped on tr.size for person and company selections (HEAD line 809). New: group clicks now set nodeId. The real regression is that a background click now only clears openId (network.js onBackgroundClick), whereas HEAD did setSelected(null). The loop therefore no longer stops on a background click. Off-screen running was already in HEAD.
confirmed.betterFix: Restore background click clearing the pick (or at least nodeId). Then gate the trail animation on IntersectionObserver plus reduced motion, as proposed.

confirmed.title: Pulse and selection flight ignore prefers-reduced-motion
confirmed.what: Only the opening swing checks prefers-reduced-motion. Every selection still flies the camera for 650 ms and pulses expanding rings for 1.1 s, with about 97 animation frames per press. The trail dash animation also runs under reduced motion.
confirmed.evidence: window.matchMedia stubbed to return matches:true. After setting highlightIds (5,000 of 30,000), 97 frames ran before the loop went idle. Code: pulse.current = performance.now() and flyTo(..., TURN_MS), with no calm check. `calm` is only read at line 1046.
confirmed.fix: Read reduced motion once (a ref). When set, use pulse.current = 0, jump the camera (ms 0), and draw the trail without lineDashOffset animation.
confirmed.verifierNote: Only line 1046 reads prefers-reduced-motion. The highlight effect (1072-1079) always sets pulse.current and flyTo(...,TURN_MS), and the dash offset animates by time at 635/645. The pulse is new. The flights and dash were already unguarded in HEAD. This is an accessibility polish issue, not a broken feature.

confirmed.title: Every new Set with the same people re-flies the camera and re-pulses; Find does this on each keystroke
confirmed.what: The effect keys on Set identity. In the page, Find builds a new Set on each change of findText, so typing 'stri' then 'strip' then 'stripe' (or adding a trailing space, same ids) turns the camera for 650 ms and pulses again each time. A double click on a node also fires two clicks, each calling setPick with a new Set, so it flies and pulses twice. The build report itself asks the page to keep the Set stable, but Find does not.
confirmed.evidence: Rerender with new Set(lit), same 5,000 ids: one frame was queued at once and 86 frames ran (a fresh pulse and flight). network.js: `const keys = new Set(profile.everyone.keys.filter(...))` inside a useMemo that depends on findText.
confirmed.fix: In the globe, compare the new highlight set with the previous one by size and members, and skip the turn and pulse when they are equal. Debounce the turn for Find.
confirmed.verifierNote: The selection memo depends on findText (untrimmed), so a trailing space rebuilds an identical Set and re-flies and re-pulses. A double click fires two onNodeClick calls, each making a new Set. New ids on each keystroke re-flying is arguably intended. Only the identical-set case is a defect, which makes this minor, not major.
confirmed.betterFix: Compare by size and members in the globe effect and skip when equal. Also take findText out of the memo deps (term is already trimmed and only the label uses the raw text).

confirmed.title: About 38,000 canvas calls per frame with 5,000 lit, for each animated frame
confirmed.what: The lit-dot pass runs every frame over all lit ids. For each it does a byId lookup, a place lookup, a new array from pr(), and withAlpha(HIGHLIGHT, 0.22) re-parsing the hex and building a string, then 2 to 3 arcs and fills. The pulse is 1.1 s and the flight 650 ms, and the trail loop (globe-5) is endless, so this runs continuously. I could not measure real raster cost without a browser; even the no-op canvas costs 11 to 17 ms per frame.
confirmed.evidence: jsdom, stub ctx, 30,000 people by role, 5,000 lit: first lit frame 16.6 ms, 38,213 ctx calls, 7 measureText. 97 frames to settle at 11.3 ms average. The idle frame with nothing lit was about 0 ms.
confirmed.fix: Precompute the lit points (place vectors) and the two rgba strings once per selection. Batch all lit dots into one path per fill (moveTo plus arc) instead of a beginPath and fill per dot. Draw the pulse ring only for the first few hundred dots.
confirmed.verifierNote: Lines 833-850: per lit dot there is a byId lookup, pr() allocation, withAlpha parsing per dot, and two beginPath/arc/fill pairs, about 8 calls each, so about 40k calls at 5,000 lit. This matches the reported 38k. It becomes continuous when combined with the new group-click nodeId trail loop (a 5,000-person group click). I could not measure raster cost without a browser.

confirmed.title: Clicking one person flies to a fixed zoom; from a closer view this zooms out
confirmed.what: A person click sets highlightIds to that person. spreadOf gives angle 0, so the target s is clamped to the cap 9/(PERSON_R*FRONT*kappa), where people are 9px. Before the change a person click did not move the camera. Now it jumps about 7 times in from home, and a user already zoomed closer (max 34px) is pulled back out.
confirmed.evidence: VC By role: target s 1780, maxS 6726, home about 254. By company: target 1001, maxS 3780. HEAD onNodeClick for a person only called setSelected and did not change the camera.
confirmed.fix: For a single lit person, keep the current s when it is already at or above the target (target = max(current s, fit)). Only turn the yaw and pitch.
confirmed.verifierNote: Line 1079: with angle 0, room/(FRONT*0.03) exceeds the cap, so s = 9/(PERSON_R*FRONT*kappa). This is absolute and ignores the current cam.s, so a user zoomed past it is pulled out. HEAD's person click did not move the camera.

confirmed.title: The 90% spread angle zooms in so far that up to 10% of the lit people are off screen
confirmed.what: spreadOf frames the angle that holds 90% of the points, and the camera zooms to fit only that angle. Up to 1 in 10 lit people can end up out of frame or behind the rim, while the corner count still says all of them are lit. The spec says 'a press is always visible'.
confirmed.evidence: spreadOf(91 points at [0,0,1] + 9 at [1,0,0]): angle 0.0986, share 0.0024. The camera zooms to fit 0.1 rad, so the 9 people at 90 degrees are at the rim or outside the canvas. The badge reads '100 lit'.
confirmed.fix: Use the 90% angle only to decide between near and wide. Frame using the max angle, or pull back to fit max(angle90, maxAngle) when maxAngle < WIDE threshold.
confirmed.verifierNote: spreadOf(91 at [0,0,1] plus 9 at [1,0,0]) gave angle 0.0986 and share 0.0024. The camera fits sin(0.0986)+0.03, so the 9 points at 90 degrees project about 7 times outside the room. The comment at line 1062 itself promises 'bring them all into view'.

confirmed.title: Far-side lit dots are painted on top of the near side
confirmed.what: The lit-dot pass runs after all clusters are painted and ignores depth. A far-side lit person (z<0, alpha 0.35, 3.5px amber) is drawn over near-side clusters, people and rays, so it reads as part of the cluster in front. With a wide selection (globe-2) the front of the globe gets amber dots belonging to people behind it.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 832-852: the forEach over lit runs after `for (const [child, cq] of tops) paint(child, cq)`. Only alpha differs by `front`. There is no occlusion test and no draw before the front hemisphere.
confirmed.fix: Draw back-side lit dots before painting the front-facing tops (split tops by hz sign), and front-side dots after.
confirmed.verifierNote: The lit-dot loop (832-852) runs after the depth-sorted paint at line 827 with no depth split. Far-side dots (alpha 0.35) are drawn over near-side clusters. Confirmed by reading only.

confirmed.title: Light-theme lit amber is under 3:1 against the canvas
confirmed.what: THEMES.light.lit is #F59E0B on bg #F8FAFC, a contrast of about 2.06:1. That is below the 3:1 needed for non-text graphics. The 2.4px lit dot and the 2px ring are the only signal of a selection when zoomed out.
confirmed.evidence: Relative luminance of #F59E0B is about 0.438, of #F8FAFC about 0.955: (0.955+0.05)/(0.438+0.05) = 2.06.
confirmed.fix: Use a deeper amber for the light theme (for example the amber-600/700 family, at least 3:1 on #F8FAFC) inside THEMES.light.lit.
confirmed.verifierNote: Computed luminance #F59E0B 0.438 and #F8FAFC 0.955, ratio 2.06:1. Pre-existing: HEAD had HIGHLIGHT = '#F59E0B' (HEAD line 27). Now moved into THEMES.light.lit unchanged.

confirmed.title: Lit ids not in the atlas make rays brighter and hide names, with no count
confirmed.what: When highlightIds is non-empty but none of its ids are on the globe, hasLit is true but litCount is 0, so dimLevels returns 1 for everything. Faded rays then use D.ray*2 = 2 and D.ray*1.6 = 1.6 alpha, brighter than the normal 0.7/0.55. All person names are suppressed (!(hasLit && !isLit)) and no badge shows. The page filters keys to the atlas today, so this is rare.
confirmed.evidence: highlightIds = new Set(['p:nobody']): no 'lit' badge, effect returns early. In draw, hasLit = true, D = {ray:1,...}, so arc alpha = 1*2.
confirmed.fix: In draw, define hasLit as litCount > 0 (pass litCount through live.current) instead of lit.size.
confirmed.verifierNote: hasLit = lit.size (line 541) while dims come from litCount (line 385). With unknown ids D = all 1, so line 822 gives arc alpha D.ray*2 = 2 against a normal 0.7, and names are suppressed. This is reachable when a pick's keys survive a source or 'direct only' filter that removes those people: pick keys are not re-filtered to the atlas.

confirmed.title: The 'N lit' badge sits where sticky group banners are drawn
confirmed.what: The badge is absolutely placed at right-3 top-3, about 12 to 32px from the top. Sticky group labels are drawn at y = 18 and clamped only against the left zoom buttons (bx up to w - bw - 4). A banner for a right-hand cluster is drawn under the badge, and on a phone-width canvas this is likely. I could not see it without a browser.
confirmed.evidence: Line 904: bx = clamp(l.x - bw/2, l.y < 160 ? 52 : 4, Math.max(52, w - bw - 4)). stickY = 18 + (depth-1)*27. Nothing reserves the top-right corner.
confirmed.fix: Reserve the badge's box in `taken` before labels are placed, or clamp sticky labels to w - badgeWidth - 8 when litCount > 0.
confirmed.verifierNote: By code reading only. The DOM badge sits at right-3 top-3 (line 1260). Sticky labels at stickY = 18 are clamped only to w-bw-4 (line 904), and `taken` does not reserve the badge box. I could not confirm visually without a browser.

confirmed.title: With two top clusters the second is placed exactly behind the first
confirmed.what: greedy picks the spot with the most room, which for the second cluster is the antipode of the first. A two-bucket file (for example By tag with two tags) opens with half the network directly behind the other half. This is inherited from the old placement, but placeClusters now owns it. Under By role on the VC sample, 3 of 4 groups are on the back.
confirmed.evidence: placeClusters([40, 30.8]) gives centres[1] = [-0.04, -0.02, -1]. VC By role puts Operators 164, Investors 112 and Experts 65 at z<0.
confirmed.fix: Limit candidate spots for the first few clusters to the hemisphere facing the home camera, as long as they fit there.
confirmed.verifierNote: placeClusters([40,30.8]) gives centres[1] = [-0.039,-0.024,-0.999]. VC By role: Operators 164 at z=-1.00. Founder By role: Founders 180 at z=-1. This is the root cause of globe-1, and the greedy rule is inherited from HEAD.

confirmed.title: A typed answer lights only the first 100 people while the chip lights all
confirmed.what: scoreContacts cuts results at MAX_RESULTS=100. The page builds the selection, the globe lighting, Copy and CSV from answer.results (network.js:575-582). The page's own example question "Which investors do I know?" says "Answer · 112" but lights and lists 100, while the "112 investors" chip lights 112. A typed role question never matches its chip once a family has more than 100 people.
confirmed.evidence: Example questions: vc "Which investors do I know?" card=112, total=112, results=100. crm "Which sales and marketing people do I know?" 102/100. founder file "Which engineers do I know?" 201/100. "Which senior leaders do I know?" on vc: total 201, 100 lit.
confirmed.fix: Return every matching key for role, tag, place, industry and date answers (or the full key list next to the capped rows), and build the selection from that list.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: vc "Which investors do I know?" total=112 res=100; fo engineers 201/100; crm sales and marketing 102/100; vc senior 201/100. network.js:579 builds the selection keys from answer.results only. The engineers' own ask test passes limit Infinity, so it never catches the cap.
confirmed.betterFix: For non-intro answers return `keys` (every match's contact key) next to the capped rows and build the selection from keys. Intro paths also take total from the capped direct list (query.js:948), so apply the same fix there.

confirmed.title: The model is called, and overrides the rules, when the rules found a lens
confirmed.what: `specific` leaves out filters.lens. So "who can help me raise" and "diligence on Stripe" still go to the model even though the rules read them. The model's filters then replace the rules' reading, which breaks the rule that the model is called only when the rules find nothing. The page shows "question read by AI".
confirmed.evidence: With useLlm true and chatComplete mocked: "who can help me raise" gives calls=1, parsedBy=llm. The same happens for "diligence on Stripe" and "warm intro please".
confirmed.fix: Add `|| rules.lens` to `specific` at line 562.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced with chatComplete mocked: "who can help me raise", "diligence on Stripe" and "warm intro please" each give calls=1 and parsedBy=llm, and the model's filters replace the lens (lens=null). query.js:562-564 leaves out rules.lens.

confirmed.title: "Intro paths" buttons send company names from the file to the model
confirmed.what: PeoplePanel's Intro paths button (PeoplePanel.js:68, 282) asks "Intro paths to {c.company}" through askExample. cleanEntity rejects a company name over six words or made only of stopwords. The rules then find nothing and the app-built text, which carries a company name from the user's file, goes to the model without the user typing it.
confirmed.evidence: Contact company "Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board of Trustees Canada": the model received "Intro paths to Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board of Trustees Canada". Company "The Who": the model received "Intro paths to The Who". In both cases intent=general and no intro section was shown.
confirmed.fix: Call the API with `target: company` (already supported, parsedBy 'target') instead of building a question, so no file value can reach parseQuestion.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: company "Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board of Trustees Canada" and "The Who" make answerQuestion send "Intro paths to <company>" to the model (calls=1, intent general). network.js:729 builds the question from c.company and PeoplePanel's button calls it. The route already accepts `target`.

confirmed.title: Negation returns the opposite set, with no note
confirmed.what: Nothing reads "not", "except" or "without". The words are dropped and the remaining filter is applied, so the user gets exactly the people they asked to exclude, and the chips under the answer show no sign of it.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "not at Google" gives 19, the people AT Google. "everyone except investors" gives the 112 investors. crm: "customers not churned" gives 116, including the 45 churned. lp: "investors not in New York" gives the 10 in New York.
confirmed.fix: Detect not/except/without/excluding before a company, role, tag or place and either apply it as an exclusion or return a note that exclusions are not understood, with no results.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: vc "not at Google" gives 19, the people at Google. "everyone except investors" gives 112 investors. crm "customers not churned" gives 116. lp "investors not in New York" gives 10. No note is added in any case.

confirmed.title: A date phrase after a company is swallowed into the company name
confirmed.what: The cleanEntity split list has no date words (recently, last, this, since, connected, before). The company becomes "Stripe recently", which matches nobody.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "Who do I know at Stripe recently", "... at Stripe last year" and "... at Stripe this year?" each give 0, read as "At Stripe recently" and so on. "engineers at Google connected in 2016" gives 0, read as "At Google connected". "Who do I know at Stripe since 2020" gives 0. By contrast "at Stripe in 2016" gives 1.
confirmed.fix: Add recent(ly), last, past, this, since, before, after, connected, added, met and a 4-digit year to the split alternation in cleanEntity.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: "at Stripe recently", "at Stripe last year" and "at Stripe since 2020" each give 0, read as "At Stripe recently" and so on. "engineers at Google connected in 2016" is read as "At Google connected" and gives 0. "at Stripe in 2016" gives 1. The split list at cleanEntity line 141 has no date words.

confirmed.title: A city typed alone returns nobody
confirmed.what: A bare place falls through to the keyword fallback. Keywords are tested only against title, company and tags, never location, so the user sees "No one in your network matches that" for a city that has a chip.
confirmed.evidence: crm: "New York" gives 0 (the chip says 63), "Toronto" gives 0 (chip 58), "Austin" gives 0 ("in Austin" gives 49). lp: "Chicago" gives 0.
confirmed.fix: In the fallback, match a word or phrase against the file's cityOf values (knownLocations) and turn it into a location filter, or include location in the keyword text.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: crm "New York" gives 0 (Mentions new; Mentions york) against a 63 chip. "Toronto" gives 0 against a 58 chip, "Austin" gives 0, lp "Chicago" gives 0. The keyword text at line 770 has no location.

confirmed.title: A bare company name is read as an OR of its words or as an industry
confirmed.what: Without "at", a company name is split into separate keywords matched with OR, or one word hits a KEYWORD_GROUP, so the answer is several times wider than the company chip.
confirmed.evidence: crm: "Marlowe Department Stores" gives 56, read as Mentions marlowe/department/stores (the chip says 18). "Bayview Health System" gives 80, read as "Mentions healthcare" (the chip says 16).
confirmed.fix: Before the keyword fallback, check the remaining text against the file's company names (groupByCompany labels) and read a match as a company filter.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: crm "Marlowe Department Stores" gives 56, three OR-ed keywords, against an 18 chip. "Bayview Health System" gives 80 as Mentions healthcare, against a 16 chip. Both names are shortcut chips on this file.

confirmed.title: A company after "in" is read as a place
confirmed.what: locRe takes any capitalised words after in/near as a location without checking the file's cities or companies, so a company becomes a place and the answer is 0. On LinkedIn files it also adds the wrong note that locations are missing.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "who do I know in Stripe" gives 0, read as "In Stripe". "people in Goldman Sachs" gives 0, read as "In Goldman Sachs". Both companies have 22 and 12 people.
confirmed.fix: When the captured phrase equals a company in the file (normalizeCompanyKey match) and is not a city in the file, read it as a company.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: vc "who do I know in Stripe" and "people in Goldman Sachs" each give 0, read as a place. Both add the wrong LinkedIn "no location" note, while the file has 22 Stripe and 12 Goldman Sachs contacts.

confirmed.title: "in the UK" and "the United Kingdom" return nobody
confirmed.what: shortLoc allows "the" only before "bay area", and locRe needs a capital letter straight after "in". So "in the UK" falls to the lower-case path, which fails the known-locations check because location text says "United Kingdom", and then becomes the keyword uk.
confirmed.evidence: crm: "Who is in the UK" gives 0 (Mentions uk). "people in the United Kingdom" gives 0 (Mentions united; Mentions kingdom). "people in UK" gives 49.
confirmed.fix: Strip a leading "the" before both place regexes, and send the lower-case path through LOCATION_ALIASES before the known-locations check.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: crm "Who is in the UK" gives 0 (Mentions uk). "people in the United Kingdom" gives 0. "people in UK" gives 49.

confirmed.title: Tags that are stopwords ("warm") are ignored, widening the answer
confirmed.what: STOPWORDS (line 120) contains warm, intro, contact, network and friends, and the plain-tag loop skips any tag that is a stopword. The LP file has a "15 tagged “warm”" chip, but typing warm does nothing.
confirmed.evidence: lp: "warm" gives 0 with "Ask about a company...". "warm investors" gives all 114. "warm LPs" gives 114. The chip "tagged “warm”" typed back gives 15.
confirmed.fix: For tags from the file, do not apply the STOPWORDS skip, or apply it only to words that are not in vocab.tags.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: lp "warm" gives 0 and the "Ask about a company" note. "warm investors" gives all 114. "warm LPs" gives 114 through the lens. "tagged “warm”" gives 15, the chip's number. Line 254 skips the tag because STOPWORDS contains warm.

confirmed.title: Several tags are OR-ed, while combined chips are AND-ed
confirmed.what: Any one tag counts as a hit. Pressing the "churned" and "customer" chips together gives their intersection (spec section 2), but asking for churned customers gives the union, so the totals disagree.
confirmed.evidence: crm: "churned customers" gives 116 (73 customer + 45 churned, union). "prospects and customers" gives 171. "customers not churned" gives 116.
confirmed.fix: Require every named tag (`f.tags.every`) unless the question joins them with "or".
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: crm "churned customers" gives 116, the union, where the two chips pressed together give the intersection. The fix as proposed is wrong for "prospects and customers": in plain English that means both groups, and the fix would AND them.
confirmed.betterFix: AND the tags when one tag word modifies another ("churned customers": an adjacent tag before a plural tag). Keep OR for lists joined by and/or/commas, and show "Tagged A or B" against "Tagged A and B" in the understood chips so the reading is visible.

confirmed.title: "nurses", "surgeons" and "doctors" return the whole clinician family
confirmed.what: The doctors group has a family but no `title` test, so every clinician word counts all clinicians, and the answer chip reads "Doctors" even for a question about clinicians or nurses.
confirmed.evidence: healthcare: "nurses" gives 100 (21 titles say nurse). "surgeons" gives 100. "which nurses do I know" is read as "Doctors". crm: "any doctors?" gives 74, including Nurse Practitioners.
confirmed.fix: Keep "clinicians" on the family. Give doctor, nurse and surgeon words their own groups with a `title` test inside the family, as designers are.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: hc "nurses", "surgeons" and "which nurses do I know" each give all 100 clinicians, labelled Doctors. crm "any doctors?" gives 74, the whole clinician family. Line 73 has a family and no title test.

confirmed.title: "head of product", "VPs" and "managing directors" return every executive
confirmed.what: The executives ask regex swallows "heads? of", "vps?" and "directors?" and matches the whole executives title set. "head of product" never reaches the product group, and "VPs" includes chiefs, directors and heads.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "head of product" gives 179 (Executives). "VPs" gives 179. "managing directors" gives 179. crm: the same questions give 192 of 328.
confirmed.fix: Test the product group before executives for "head of product", and give VPs and managing directors their own title tests.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: vc "head of product", "VPs" and "managing directors" each give 179, Executives. crm "head of product" gives 192.

confirmed.title: "senior people at Meta" ignores "senior"
confirmed.what: The senior group's ask needs "senior leaders" or "c-suite". "senior people", "senior folks" and "seniors" are dropped silently, so the answer is the whole company.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "senior people at Meta" gives 11, read only as "At Meta", which is every Meta contact.
confirmed.fix: Extend the ask to `senior\s+(?:leaders?|leadership|people|folks|staff)|seniors?` before the company is cut.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: vc "senior people at Meta" gives 11, read only as "At Meta". This is the same 11 as "who do I know at Meta".

confirmed.title: "LPs", "allocators", "endowments" and "family offices" return the raise lens, not allocators
confirmed.what: No role group matches the lp role (spec section 7 makes pension, endowment and family-office staff allocators). These words trigger the raise lens, which also returns investors and bankers.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "LPs" gives 131 while the lp role covers 9 people. lp file: "LPs" gives 114 and "endowment staff" gives 114, while the lp role covers 89.
confirmed.fix: Add a ROLE_GROUP {label:'allocators', ask: /LPs?|limited partners|allocators?|endowments?|pensions?|family offices?/} that matches classifyContact(c).role === 'lp'.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: vc "LPs" gives 131 through the lens. lp "LPs" and "endowment staff" each give all 114. No ROLE_GROUP maps to the classifier's lp role (roles.js:30).

confirmed.title: "last month", "last week" and "past year" are not read as dates
confirmed.what: lastRe needs either "the" or a number, so the most common short forms fall to the keywords "last" and "month" and return 0. With the model on, they are sent to it.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "last month" gives 0 (Mentions last; Mentions month). "last week" gives 0. "people I connected with past year" gives 0. "in the last month" gives 7. "last month connections" with useLlm gives calls=1.
confirmed.fix: Make the count optional in the second alternative: `\b(?:last|past)\s+(?:(\d{1,3}|[a-z-]+)\s+)?(days?|weeks?|months?|years?)`. Keep the special "last year" calendar rule first.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: "last month", "last week" and "people I connected with past year" each give 0 as keywords. "in the last month" gives 7. With the model on, "last month connections" gives calls=1. lastRe (line 415) needs "the" or a count.

confirmed.title: People's names cannot be asked about; the answer says nobody matches
confirmed.what: The keyword fallback tests title, company and tags, never the name. A question about a person in the file returns "No one in your network matches that", and with the model on, the name is sent to it.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "who knows Oakley Merriweather" gives 0. "find Parker" gives 0. "Who is Quinn Hawksley" gives 0. All three people are in the file.
confirmed.fix: Include c.name in the fallback text, or recognise a full name from the file before the fallback and return that person.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: "who knows Oakley Merriweather", "find Parker" and "Who is Quinn Hawksley" each give 0. With the model on, calls=1. The page has a separate Find box (network.js selection, term filter) that does match names, so the user has a working route; severity is overstated. The name sent to the model is text the user typed, which the rules allow.

confirmed.title: Plural words in the fallback match nothing
confirmed.what: Fallback keywords are matched whole-word as typed, with no singular form, so a plural misses every title written in the singular.
confirmed.evidence: healthcare: "cardiologists" gives 0 while titles say "Cardiologist". lp: "pensions" gives 0 while "pension" gives 17.
confirmed.fix: Match each fallback word as `singular(word)` plus optional s/es (reuse tagRe-style forms).
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: hc "cardiologists" gives 0 and "cardiologist" gives 15. lp "pensions" gives 0 and "pension" gives 17.

confirmed.title: Unrecognised words are dropped once any filter is found
confirmed.what: The keyword fallback runs only when nothing else was recognised. A place or role found anywhere makes the rest of the question vanish silently, and the chips under the answer do not show what was dropped.
confirmed.evidence: lp: "pension funds in Seattle" gives 14, every Seattle contact, read only as "In Seattle". crm: "customers in New York and Boston" gives 16, with New York only.
confirmed.fix: Keep the leftover meaningful words as keywords (AND) or add a note naming the words that were ignored.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: lp "pension funds in Seattle" gives 14, the same as "in Seattle". crm "customers in New York and Boston" gives 16, with Boston dropped (understood shows only New York). Line 344 runs the fallback only when nothing was found.

confirmed.title: Companies after "of" or "on" are dropped
confirmed.what: COMPANY_PATTERNS need at, @, for or with. "CEO of X" and "diligence on X" lose the company, so the answer covers the whole network.
confirmed.evidence: crm: "Who is the CEO of Marlowe Department Stores" gives 29, every CEO (understood: Ceos). crm: "diligence on Stripe" gives 328 of 328 by the rules.
confirmed.fix: Add `\b(?:of|on|into)\s+(.+)$` as a company pattern when the captured phrase matches a company in the file.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: crm "Who is the CEO of Marlowe Department Stores" gives 29, every CEO (Ceos). crm "diligence on Stripe" gives 328, the whole file.

confirmed.title: The old-export recent chip's label returns nobody when typed
confirmed.what: On a file whose newest date is more than 60 days old, the chip reads "connected in the 12 months before this export". lastRe needs "the last" or "the past", so the chip's own words do not parse.
confirmed.evidence: small file: the chip "7 connected in the 12 months before this export" typed back gives 0 (Mentions 12, months, before, export). The parity check "Who connected in the 12 months before this export?" gives got=0, missing=7.
confirmed.fix: Recognise "(the )?N months before this export" as {kind:'last', months:N}.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: on the small file the chip reads "7 connected in the 12 months before this export". Its words typed back, with or without "Who", give 0 as four keywords.

confirmed.title: Intro paths to a company with "in" or "with" in its name go to the wrong company
confirmed.what: cleanEntity cuts at " in ", " with " and " as ", so a company name containing these words is cut short and the intro is run for that fragment.
confirmed.evidence: Contact at "Partners In Health": the Intro paths button gives intent=intro-path, target="Partners", total=0.
confirmed.fix: Use the target parameter from the button (see ask-3), and do not cut a captured phrase that equals a company in the file.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: company "Partners In Health" with "Intro paths to Partners In Health" gives intent intro-path, target "Partners", total 0.

confirmed.title: Several date forms are misread or ignored
confirmed.what: Quarters, ranges, bare years and years before 1990 are not read. A quarter is even read as a place.
confirmed.evidence: vc: "in Q1 2025" gives 0, read as "In Q" with the LinkedIn location note. "between 2020 and 2022" gives 0 (keywords). "my 2024 connections" and "2024" give 0. "connected in 1985" gives keyword 1985. "people from 2024" is read as since 2024.
confirmed.fix: Add rules for between Y1 and Y2, Qn YYYY and a bare year next to connections, and keep 'Q1' out of locRe.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: "in Q1 2025" gives 0, read as "In Q" with the LinkedIn note. "between 2020 and 2022" gives keywords. "my 2024 connections" gives Mentions 2024. "connected in 1985" gives a keyword. "people from 2024" is read as since 2024, giving 150.

confirmed.title: "this year" and "this month" use the server's clock, not the user's
confirmed.what: The page sends no `today`, and dayOf(new Date()) reads the server's local date (UTC on a typical host). On 31 December after 4pm Pacific, "this year" means the new year and returns 0. The same applies to "this month" at month end.
confirmed.evidence: network.js:695-703 sends only { question } or contacts. parseConnected computes `now = dayOf(today || new Date())`. answerQuestion is called from the route without today.
confirmed.fix: Send the browser's local YYYY-MM-DD as `today` in the request body and pass it through the route to answerQuestion.
confirmed.verifierNote: network.js:695-703 sends only question (plus contacts when signed out). The route (api/network/query.js) calls answerQuestion without today. parseConnected calls dayOf(new Date()), which uses the server's local getFullYear/getMonth (line 388), so at a year or month boundary the server's date is used rather than the user's.

confirmed.title: Answer chips show "Ceos", "Doctors" for clinicians, and lower-case places
confirmed.what: understoodOf capitalises the group's internal label, so the chip under the answer does not repeat the user's words or the page's family names.
confirmed.evidence: "CEOs" is shown as "Ceos". "Which clinicians do I know?" and "100 clinicians" are shown as "Doctors". "who is in london" is shown as "In london". "who's at google" is shown as "At google".
confirmed.fix: Store a display label per group (CEOs, CTOs, CFOs, clinicians), and show the file's own spelling for cities and companies.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: understood shows "Ceos" for CEOs and "Doctors" for "Which clinicians do I know?" (on the healthcare example question whose chip says clinicians). It also shows "In london" and "At google".

confirmed.title: "University Hospital" staff counted as Education; half of the healthcare file's Education chip is wrong
confirmed.what: On the healthcare sample the first-screen chip reads "58 in Education", but 29 of those 58 people work at "X University Hospital": physicians, nurses, surgeons and a CSO. The known-employer list matches the word 'university' before any hospital word, so every university hospital is put in Education. The same read-out says "Strongest in Healthcare (165)".

confirmed.title: Self-employed, Stealth, Retired, N/A are treated as companies and lead the read-out

confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced with a generated file. confirmed.title: Common company spellings are not merged (McKinsey, Google/Alphabet, Meta/Facebook, JPMorgan)
confirmed.what: The spec says company chips count companies merged across spellings. normalizeCompanyKey only strips legal suffixes, so 'McKinsey & Company' and 'McKinsey' are separate companies, and so are Google/Alphabet, Meta/Meta Platforms/Facebook, Amazon/AWS/'Amazon Web Services (AWS)' and JPMorgan Chase & Co./J.P. Morgan/JP Morgan. Company chips undercount and can name the wrong largest company.
confirmed.evidence: normalizeCompanyKey: 'McKinsey & Company'->'mckinsey and company', 'McKinsey'->'mckinsey', 'JPMorgan Chase & Co.'->'jpmorgan chase and' (dangling 'and'), 'J.P. Morgan'->'j p morgan' (industry Other), 'Alphabet Inc.'->'alphabet'. groupByCompany gave Google:3, Alphabet:2, McKinsey:1, McKinsey & Company:1, Meta:1, Meta Platforms:1, Facebook:1 as separate groups. Profile chip: '6 at McKinsey & Company' while 4 more are at 'McKinsey'.
confirmed.fix: Drop a trailing 'company'/'and company'/'and co' tail and a parenthesised acronym when grouping, and add a small alias table (alphabet->google, facebook/meta platforms->meta, aws->amazon, j p morgan/jpmorgan chase->jpmorgan) used by companyKeyFor.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: 'McKinsey & Company' gives the key 'mckinsey and company', 'JPMorgan Chase & Co.' gives 'jpmorgan chase and', 'J.P. Morgan' gives 'j p morgan' (industry Finance & operations), and 'Alphabet Inc.' gives 'alphabet'. The chips read '6 at McKinsey & Company' and '4 at Alphabet', and Google is counted separately.
confirmed.betterFix: Strip a trailing 'and'/'and co'/'and company' after the legal suffixes. Put a small alias map inside normalizeCompanyKey so the server question engine (companyMatch) and the chips agree. An alias added only in companyKeyFor would make the question counts differ from the chip counts.

confirmed.title: Spelled-out "Vice President" ranks as a top leader; senior chip and sort order inflated
confirmed.what: readSeniority checks `president` for rank 0 before the VP check and has no lookbehind for 'vice'. So every 'Vice President …' is rank 0, the same rank as a founder or CEO. 'Chief of Staff', 'Principal Engineer', 'Principal Scientist', 'Partner Manager', 'Product Owner' and 'Associate Partner' are also rank 0. This inflates the '{n} senior leaders' chip, and 'most senior first' (the default order of every list) puts them beside CEOs.
confirmed.evidence: seniority(): 'Vice President, M&A' 0, 'Principal Engineer' 0, 'Principal Product Manager' 0, 'Partner Manager' 0, 'Chief of Staff' 0, 'Product Owner' 0, 'Director of Engineering' 1. VC sample: the '201 senior leaders' chip includes Chief of Staff 8, Vice President M&A 5, Principal Scientist 4 and Associate Partner 4 (about 10% of the chip).
confirmed.fix: Add (?<!vice )(?<!senior vice )(?<!executive vice ) before president in the rank-0 regex. Require 'principal' and 'partner' to stand alone or as a partner title (not 'Principal Engineer' or 'Partner Manager'), and drop 'chief of staff' and 'product owner' from rank 0.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced with seniority(): 'Vice President, M&A', 'Vice President of Sales', 'Senior Vice President', 'Principal Engineer', 'Partner Manager', 'Chief of Staff', 'Product Owner' and 'Associate Partner' all return 0. The VC file shows '201 senior leaders' under More. atlas.js:88 has no lookbehind for 'vice', although roles.js does have one for founders.
confirmed.betterFix: Reuse the lookbehinds from roles.js for 'president'. Check 'vice president|svp|evp' as rank 1 before the rank-0 test. For 'Product Owner', require 'owner' not preceded by 'product'.

confirmed.title: Partner Manager, Founding Engineer and "... to the CEO" titles get the wrong family
confirmed.what: Common big-tech and startup titles are misread. 'Partner Manager', 'Partner Marketing Manager', 'Channel Partner Manager' and 'Strategic Partner Development' become 'partners at professional firms'. 'Founding Engineer' and 'Founding Account Executive' become 'founders and CEOs'. 'Chief of Staff to the CEO' and 'Executive Assistant to the CEO' become founders. On a startup or big-tech network these inflate the founders chip and create a bogus 'partners at professional firms' family.
confirmed.evidence: classifyContact: 'Partner Manager | Google' -> role partner, family partners; 'Partner Marketing Manager | HubSpot' -> partners; 'Founding Engineer | Acme' -> founder/founders; 'Founding Account Executive | Acme' -> founders; 'Chief of Staff to the CEO | Acme' -> founders; 'Executive Assistant to the CEO | Acme' -> founders. 'Head of People | Acme' -> leaders (catch-all, never shown).
confirmed.fix: Partner role: match only a bare partner title (not followed by manager/marketing/development, not preceded by channel/strategic). Founder: drop 'founding' when followed by a function word, and ignore 'ceo' after 'to the'. TITLE_FAMILY people: add 'head of people'.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced with classifyContact. 'Partner Manager'@Google and 'Partner Marketing Manager'@HubSpot give partner/partners. 'Founding Engineer', 'Founding Account Executive', 'Chief of Staff to the CEO' and 'Executive Assistant to the CEO' give founder/founders. 'Head of People' gives executive/leaders (the catch-all).

confirmed.title: Industry is taken from job-function words in the title, misfiling finance staff and splitting companies
confirmed.what: Step 3 runs sector terms over the title. Any CFO, 'VP Finance' or 'Head of Payments' at an unknown company becomes Fintech, and engineers become 'Software' or 'Security' even when the employer's name says otherwise. Under By industry, and in the 'in {sector}' chips, people at one company are spread across sectors.
confirmed.evidence: industryOf: 'Chief Financial Officer | Acme Corp' -> Fintech, 'VP Finance | Northwind' -> Fintech, 'Head of Security | Northwind' -> Security. VC sample: 'Software Engineer @ Pioneer Robotics' -> Software but 'VP of Engineering @ Zephyr Robotics' -> Industrials; 'Software Engineer @ Umbra Security' -> Software vs others there -> Security. Companies split across 2+ industries: VC 9/255, founder 12/213, CRM 13/147.
confirmed.fix: Read sector terms from the company name (and tags) first and the title only when the company gives nothing. Exclude function words (financial, finance, security, software) when they come from the title.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced with industryOf: 'Chief Financial Officer'@'Acme Corp' gives Fintech, 'VP Finance'@Northwind gives Fintech, 'Head of Security'@Northwind gives Security. 'Software Engineer'@'Pioneer Robotics' gives Software while 'VP of Engineering'@'Zephyr Robotics' gives Industrials. Step 3 runs the sector terms over the title text (grouping.js:174).

confirmed.title: Investors at "X Partners" firms and law-firm partners get job-function industries
confirmed.what: COMPANY_WORD_INDUSTRY has no 'partners' word for Venture capital. Rows: 'Associate | Acme Partners -> Finance & operations', 'Partner | Juniper Partners -> Investing', 'Partner | Kirkland & Ellis -> lawyers / Investing' (the other 4 Kirkland rows -> 'Legal & policy').

'Associate'@'Acme Partners' gives Finance & operations and 'Partner'@'Juniper Partners' gives Investing. 'Partner'@'Kirkland & Ellis' is in the lawyers family but its industry is Investing.

confirmed.title: Notes column is stored as a tag, so a lightly tagged file becomes tag-led
confirmed.what: rowToContact pushes the Notes column into tags. tagProfile then counts everyone with a note as 'tagged', passes the 30% rule, and the file opens By tag, with one bubble per note sentence. The CSV export also mixes the notes into the Tags column.
confirmed.evidence: 100 rows, Tags 'hot' x8 and 'cold' x7 (15% tagged), every row has a Notes sentence: tagProfile filled=100, signal=true; defaultGrouping='tag'; read-out drops the family sentence ('100 contacts at 40 companies.', 'By tag: 8 hot, 7 cold.'); By tag buckets: hot 8, cold 7, then 12 bubbles 'Note number 15 about the call:1'..., 'Other tags:73'; listCsv Tags cell 'hot; Note number 0 about the call'.
confirmed.fix: Keep notes in their own field (contact.notes), not in tags. If that is not possible, exclude it from tagsOf, tagProfile and the tag buckets.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: with 15% real tags and a Notes column on every row, tagProfile gives filled=100, signal=true, and defaultGrouping is 'tag'. The read-out is '100 contacts at 40 companies. By tag: 8 hot, 7 cold.', and the CSV Tags cell reads 'hot; Note number 0 about the call'. parseContacts.js:387-388 pushes the notes into tags.

confirmed.title: LinkedIn metro-area locations become made-up countries and broken cities
confirmed.what: readCountry returns the last part as the country when it looks like a proper noun. LinkedIn's own metro strings become their own 'countries' under By place, and placeLevel counts them as extra countries, which can flip a US file to country level. 'Bay Area' is cut to the city 'Bay' and the country 'Bay'.
confirmed.evidence: countryOf: 'Greater Houston'->'Houston', 'Greater Philadelphia'->'Philadelphia', 'Miami-Fort Lauderdale Area'->'Miami-Fort Lauderdale', 'Washington DC-Baltimore Area'->'Washington DC-Baltimore', 'Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex'->itself, 'Salt Lake City Metropolitan Area'->'Salt Lake City', 'Remote'->'Remote', 'Bangalore Urban'->itself. cityOf('Bay Area')='Bay', countryOf='Bay'. 'Brooklyn, NY' and 'Manhattan, New York' are not merged with New York.
confirmed.fix: Treat an unrecognised single-part location as Unknown country, not as a country; add the common US metro names to the US set; resolve CITY_ALIASES before stripping 'area', so 'bay area' still matches.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced with countryOf/cityOf: 'Greater Houston' gives Houston as both country and city, 'Miami-Fort Lauderdale Area' gives Miami-Fort Lauderdale, 'Remote' gives Remote, and 'Bay Area' gives Bay/Bay. 'Brooklyn, NY' gives the city Brooklyn, not New York. 'San Francisco Bay Area' and 'Greater New York City Area' are read correctly.

confirmed.title: In tag-led files the role chip never appears, not even under More
confirmed.what: The six shown chips fill with tag(3), company(2) and place(1). 'More' is then filled type by type in plan order: remaining tags, companies and places reach the 12-chip cap before role is reached. On the sales CRM there is no role chip anywhere, yet the second example question is 'Which sales and marketing people do I know?' (from pools.role[0]). Spec section 4 puts role (1) right after place and section 6 asks for a role question only when a role chip exists.
confirmed.evidence: sales-crm.csv: shortcuts ['107 tagged prospect','73 tagged customer','69 tagged partner','18 at Marlowe Department Stores','16 at Bayview Health System','63 in New York']; more ['62 tagged decision maker','57 tagged champion','45 tagged churned','14 at Greenfield Grocers','12 at Northgate Pharmacy Group','58 in Toronto']. No role chip; question 'Which sales and marketing people do I know?' count 102.
confirmed.fix: Fill More in the plan's interleaved order (one per type per round, starting with the types that got no slot), or reserve a More slot for role. Build the role question only from a chip that is shown or in More.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced on sales-crm.csv. The shown and More chips (12) are tags, companies and places only, with no role chip. The questions still include 'Which sales and marketing people do I know?' (102), because insights.js falls back to pools.role[0] when no role chip is shown. The More loop fills type by type in plan order, so role is never reached.

confirmed.title: profileNetwork misses the 200 ms budget in the order the page runs it; the test hides it
confirmed.what: The page calls profileNetwork(visibleContacts) before buildAtlas, so it runs cold, with every classifier cache empty. At 30,000 contacts that took 285 ms, and 226-253 ms on freshly fetched contact objects (every reload or re-import). The data test passes only because it builds the atlas first and takes the best of two runs, which does not match the page.
confirmed.evidence: Generated 30,000 contacts in Jest: profileCold 285 ms, profileWarm 63 ms, profileOnFreshObjects 253 ms / 226 ms; buildAtlas role 200 ms cold. networkR2.data.test.js lines 389-397 run buildAtlas(big) before timing profileNetwork and assert Math.min(times) < 200.
confirmed.fix: Speed up the cold path (classify once per distinct title+company pair, not per object), or time the test in the page's order (profile first, cold, fresh objects) and meet 200 ms there.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced in the page's order (network.js:502 runs profileNetwork before buildAtlas at :508), with fresh objects and the same generator as the data test: 257, 375 and 237 ms, all over the 200 ms budget. The test at networkR2.data.test.js:389-397 runs buildAtlas first and takes the best of two runs.

confirmed.title: Download CSV has no UTF-8 byte-order mark; accented and non-Latin names garble in Excel
confirmed.what: listCsv returns plain UTF-8 and the Blob is created without a BOM. Excel opens such a file in the legacy code page, so names like 'Zoë 李' or 'São Paulo' show as mojibake in the file the user just downloaded.
confirmed.evidence: listCsv([{name:'Zoë 李',...}]) -> 'Name,Company,...\nZoë 李,,,,\n' (no leading ﻿); PeoplePanel.js:128 new Blob([listCsv(people)], { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8' }).
confirmed.fix: Prefix the CSV with '﻿' (in listCsv or at the Blob), and use \r\n line endings.
confirmed.verifierNote: listCsv gives 'Name\nZoë 李\n' with no BOM, and PeoplePanel.js:128 makes the Blob without one, so Excel on Windows shows mojibake. Opening the same file in Numbers, Google Sheets or Excel for Mac (which detects UTF-8) is fine. This is polish, not wrong data.

confirmed.title: "No company listed" takes one of the sixteen company bubbles under By company

confirmed.title: combine repeats a duplicated id in its label

confirmed.title: listText and listCsv tags: newlines break lines, a semicolon inside a tag is ambiguous
confirmed.what: listText does not flatten newlines, so a company with a line break splits one person over two lines in 'Copy'. listCsv joins tags with '; ', so a tag containing ';' cannot be told apart from two tags.

confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: listText gives 'x, Line\nbreak', which splits one person over two lines. listCsv gives the Tags cell 'a;b; c', so a semicolon inside a tag reads as two tags.

confirmed.title: Contact caches go stale when a contact object is edited in place
confirmed.what: classifyContact, industryOf, companyKeyFor, cityOf, seniority and personNodeId cache per object in WeakMaps with no invalidation, and tagProfile caches per array. An in-place edit keeps the old family, company, city and id. No current page path mutates contacts, so this is latent.
confirmed.evidence: c={Stripe, Software Engineer, Boston}; after setting position 'Partner', company 'Sequoia Capital', location 'London, UK' and a profileUrl: family 'engineers', industry 'Fintech', company key 'stripe', city 'Boston', id 'p:n:ann|stripe' (all unchanged). tagProfile(arr) after arr.push(...) returns the same filled count (2).
confirmed.fix: Document that contacts must be immutable, or key the caches on a content hash (title|company|location).
confirmed.verifierNote: Partly reproduced: after an in-place edit, the family stays 'engineers' and the industry stays 'Fintech'. companyKeyOf is NOT stale: it returned 'sequoia capital' after the edit, so that part of the claim is wrong. No current page path changes a contact in place, so the defect is latent.

confirmed.title: Moving the globe during a selection resets the chosen sort and the paging
confirmed.what: panelPeople depends on viewNode even when a selection is active, so any view change (the camera turning to the lit people, a spin, a zoom) makes a new list. PeoplePanel then resets its effect: the sort goes back to the default and the list shrinks back to 50 rows. A user who picks A to Z and clicks 'Show 50 more' loses both as soon as the globe moves.
confirmed.evidence: Throwaway jest test, VC sample: pressed '112 investors', then A to Z, then 'Show 50 more' (100 rows, A to Z aria-checked=true). Then act(onViewNode(first group id)). Result: 50 rows, A to Z aria-checked=false. Cause: network.js:665-668 deps [selection, viewNode, byPersonId], and PeoplePanel.js:230 useEffect(() => { setSort(null); setShown(PEOPLE_PAGE) }, [people, answer]).
confirmed.fix: When a selection is set, build panelPeople without viewNode (split it into two memos). Or reset sort and paging only when the selection's identity changes, not whenever the people array changes.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced on the VC file. After '112 investors', A to Z and 'Show 50 more', the list had 100 rows. Calling onViewNode(group) dropped it to 50 rows with A to Z unchecked. The globe's flight after every selection ends in reportView (NetworkGraph.js:514), which calls setViewId, so the reset also happens on its own after each press, not only when the user moves the globe.

The Stripe and Google examples return everything. The page lights and exports only answer.results (network.js:579, PeoplePanel.js:233).

confirmed.title: A hidden source stays hidden after Remove all and re-upload, with no chip to turn it back on

confirmed.title: Opening a person no longer shows them on the globe; prefixed answer rows give a bad id

confirmed.title: Intro-path answer title counts only direct contacts, while more are lit and exported

confirmed.title: Attio errors shown verbatim use 'token' and 'API', against the wording rule and the page's 'access code'

confirmed.fix: Reword the Attio route messages to 'access code' and drop 'API'. Or map the error codes to plain text on the page.
