This is not new: the Attio route is unmodified and HEAD network.js:585 did the same. It still breaks the wording rules every time Attio fails, and the page test never renders it.

confirmed.title: Find ignores accents: 'jose' does not find José
confirmed.what: Find uses a lower-cased substring with no accent folding, so typing a name without accents finds nobody. The founder-check matcher in the same codebase folds accents.
confirmed.evidence: Throwaway test: small sample with contacts[0].name = 'José Núñez'. Find 'jose' gives 'Find “jose” · 0'; Find 'José' gives 1.
confirmed.fix: Normalise both sides with normalize('NFKD').replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g,'') before includes().
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: with contacts[0] renamed 'José Núñez', Find 'jose' showed 'Find “jose” · 0' and Find 'José' showed 1. network.js:589 is a plain lower-cased includes.

confirmed.title: Focus falls to the page body after Clear
confirmed.what: The Clear button renders only while a selection is active, so pressing it unmounts it and keyboard focus drops to <body>. A keyboard user is sent back to the top of the page.
confirmed.evidence: Throwaway test: focused 'Clear the selection' and clicked it. document.activeElement.tagName === 'BODY'.
confirmed.fix: Move focus to the Find input or the panel heading after clearing. Or keep the button rendered and disabled.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: after focusing 'Clear the selection' and clicking it, document.activeElement was BODY.

confirmed.title: Panel title truncation hides the count for long labels
confirmed.what: The count sits inside the same truncated h3 as the label. A combined label ('tagged “prospect” · at Marlowe Department Stores · in New York') or a long Find term gets cut off with an ellipsis, and the count goes with it, especially on a phone or in the 40% panel.
confirmed.evidence: {title} · {fmt(count)}
confirmed.fix: Put the count in its own shrink-0 span outside the truncated label span.
confirmed.verifierNote: PeoplePanel.js:249-251: the count span is inside the h3 that has truncate, so a long label cuts the count off. Seen from the classes only, not rendered.

confirmed.title: Senior leaders list order matches no sort button and cannot be restored
confirmed.what: The 'senior leaders' shortcut has sort 'company' (by company size). SORTS has no such key, so no sort radio is checked. Once the user picks another sort, there is no way back to the shortcut's own order.
confirmed.evidence: Throwaway test, VC sample, More then '201 senior leaders': radios 'Most senior=false, Most recent=false, A to Z=false'. insights.js:194 sets the sort to 'company'.
confirmed.fix: Add an option for the list's own order (e.g. 'Default'), or map 'company' to a labelled sort.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: under '201 senior leaders' all three sort radios had aria-checked=false. SPEC:120 makes the shortcut's own order the default, so nothing being checked is allowed. The real problem is that once another sort is picked, nothing brings the shortcut's order back.

confirmed.title: Three-chip limit disables every chip without saying why
confirmed.what: With three chips pressed, every other chip becomes disabled and drops out of the Tab order. No text says that at most three can be combined. A disabled 0-count chip and a limit-disabled chip look the same.
confirmed.evidence: disabled={!active && ((count != null && count === 0) || full)}, where full = activeIds.length >= MAX_ACTIVE. The group has no hint text.
confirmed.fix: Show a short note ('Up to three at once') while full is true. Use aria-disabled with a title instead of disabled so the chips stay reachable.
confirmed.verifierNote: Shortcuts.js:44: once three chips are on, every other chip gets disabled={... || full}, with no text saying why. Disabled buttons leave the Tab order.

confirmed.title: Phone tap targets are around 20 to 24 px
confirmed.what: Shortcut and example chips (.chip: py-1 text-xs, about 24px) are small to tap. So are the sort radios and the Copy and Download buttons (py-0.5, about 20px), the 13px profile icon link, and the Arrange by radios (py-0.5). All are hard to hit on a phone, where the panel comes first.
confirmed.evidence: globals.css:254 .chip py-1 text-xs. PeoplePanel.js:139-140 and 273 use 'px-2 py-0.5 text-xs'. PeoplePanel.js:103-104 is a 13px icon link. network.js:916 uses 'px-2 py-0.5'.
confirmed.fix: Give these controls min-h-9 (or larger padding) below the sm breakpoint.
confirmed.verifierNote: From the classes: chips use .chip py-1 text-xs, and the sort radios, Copy/Download (PeoplePanel.js:139-140, 273) and Arrange by (network.js:916) use px-2 py-0.5 text-xs. The profile link is a 13px icon. None gets a larger target on phones.

confirmed.title: 'Hidden by the source filters' also counts people hidden by 'direct only'
confirmed.what: shownAnswer counts every match dropped by visibleContacts, which also removes firm contacts when 'My direct connections only' is on. The note blames 'the source filters above', so a user looking for a source chip to turn on finds none.
confirmed.evidence: network.js:495-498 filters by sourceFilter and directOnly. PeoplePanel.js:176: '… hidden by the source filters above.'
confirmed.fix: Say 'hidden by the filters above', or name 'My direct connections only' when it is on.
confirmed.verifierNote: visibleContacts (network.js:495) also removes firm contacts when 'direct only' is on, so shownAnswer counts them in hiddenByFilters. PeoplePanel.js:176 still says '…hidden by the source filters above.'

confirmed.title: Download is named 'network-answer.csv' for every question and fails silently
confirmed.what: Every answer downloads as network-answer.csv, whatever the question, so a second download overwrites or duplicates the first with no hint of its contents. When URL.createObjectURL is unavailable, Download does nothing and shows nothing, unlike Copy, which says 'Could not copy'.
confirmed.evidence: Throwaway test: file name 'network-answer.csv' for 'Intro paths to Stripe'. Line 127: if (typeof URL.createObjectURL !== 'function') return;
confirmed.fix: Build the file name from the question text. Show 'Could not download' when the call is not available.
confirmed.verifierNote: PeoplePanel.js:247 passes label 'answer', so fileName() gives 'network-answer.csv' for every question. The silent-failure half matters little: every supported browser has URL.createObjectURL.

confirmed.title: 'Most recent' is offered on files with no connection dates
confirmed.what: On sales-crm.csv and the LP list (no Connected On column), 'Most recent' sorts every row on an empty date, which falls back to A to Z with no message. The control looks broken.
confirmed.evidence: SORTS is fixed. byRecent compares String(connectedOn || ''), which is '' for every row in sales-crm.csv (header: Name,Company,Title,Email,Location,Tags).
confirmed.fix: Hide 'Most recent' when no listed person has connectedOn. profile.fields already knows.
confirmed.verifierNote: The sales-crm.csv and lp-fundraising-list.csv headers have no Connected On column. On those files byRecent compares '' with '', so 'Most recent' gives exactly the A to Z order.

confirmed.title: Firm-contact mark has no text for screen readers
confirmed.what: A firm-wide contact is marked only by a hollow dot with a title attribute. A screen reader announces nothing, and sighted users see only its shape and colour until they open the row. Before, results had a visible 'Firm · via X' chip.
confirmed.evidence: . HEAD ResultRow showed Firm{via}.
confirmed.fix: Add sr-only text ('firm contact') next to the dot, or a small visible 'via {name}' label.
confirmed.verifierNote: PeoplePanel.js:89: the firm mark is an empty span with only a title. HEAD:221 showed a visible 'Firm · via X' chip. SPEC asks for a hollow mark, so the mark itself is allowed, but it needs text a screen reader can read.

confirmed.title: Radio groups take one Tab stop per option and have no arrow keys
confirmed.what: 'Sort people' and 'Arrange by' use role='radiogroup' with plain buttons. Every option is its own Tab stop and the arrow keys do nothing, which breaks the radio pattern screen-reader users expect.
confirmed.evidence: PeoplePanel.js:271-274 and network.js:908-919 have role="radio" buttons with no tabIndex management and no onKeyDown.
confirmed.fix: Use aria-pressed toggle buttons, or add a roving tabIndex with arrow-key handling.
confirmed.verifierNote: PeoplePanel.js:271-274 and network.js:908-919 are role=radio buttons with no roving tabIndex and no onKeyDown, so each option is its own Tab stop and the arrow keys do nothing.

confirmed.title: Smooth scrolls ignore reduced motion
confirmed.what: After an upload and after every answer, the page scrolls with behavior 'smooth' even under prefers-reduced-motion. The globe respects that setting; the page does not.
confirmed.evidence: network.js:680 glanceRef.current?.scrollIntoView?.({ behavior: 'smooth', … }) and line 717 mapRef … 'smooth'.
confirmed.fix: Use behavior: matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth'.
confirmed.verifierNote: network.js:680 and 717 hard-code behavior 'smooth', and the file never checks prefers-reduced-motion.

confirmed.title: 'Copied' feedback is not announced, and its timer outlives the component
confirmed.what: The Copy result ('Copied' or 'Could not copy') only changes the button text. Screen readers do not announce it. The 2-second setTimeout also calls setCopied after the list (and ListActions) may have unmounted, for example when the selection becomes empty.
confirmed.evidence: setCopied('Copied') … setTimeout(() => setCopied(''), 2000). There is no role=status and no cleanup. 'if (!people.length) return null' unmounts the buttons for an empty list.
confirmed.fix: Put the message in a role='status' span. Clear the timer in an effect cleanup.
confirmed.verifierNote: PeoplePanel.js:117-124: 'Copied' only replaces the button text, with no status role. The timer has no cleanup. React 18 does not warn about a state update after unmount, so the timer half is cosmetic.

confirmed.title: Combining shortcuts is almost never possible on the VC sample
confirmed.what: Combining is the headline new interaction, yet after pressing '112 investors' on the venture file, 9 of the 11 other chips read '0 …' and are disabled (both company chips, engineers, Software and others). The spec's own example, 'investors · at Stripe', cannot happen on this file. The user mostly sees a row of greyed-out zeros.
confirmed.evidence: Throwaway test, VC sample, after 'role:investors' the enabled chips are only: '112 investors | 17 connected in the last 12 months | 78 senior leaders'.
confirmed.fix: While a chip is active, hide the 0-count chips instead of greying them out. Or rank 'More' chips by their overlap with the active chip.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced: after 'role:investors', 3 of 12 chips stay enabled. SPEC:61 requires a chip that would leave nobody to be disabled, so the proposed fix of hiding them goes against the spec.
confirmed.betterFix: Keep zero-count chips disabled as the spec says. While a chip is on, rank the More chips by how many people they share with it, and swap in the top overlapping ones so the user sees chips that can actually be combined.

confirmed.title: 'Everything stays private to you' is not true signed out: each question posts the contacts
confirmed.what: The empty state promises privacy. Signed out, every question sends every contact (name, company, title, location, profile URL, tags, connection date) to /api/network/query. The server does not store them and no model sees them, but they do leave the browser.
confirmed.evidence: network.js:696-702 sets body.contacts = contacts.map(...) when mode !== 'saved'. network.js:814 says 'Everything stays private to you.'
confirmed.fix: Say 'Your contacts are never stored or shared; questions are answered on our server'. Or answer signed-out questions in the browser.
confirmed.verifierNote: network.js:696-702: signed out, every question posts all contacts to /api/network/query, and line 814 says 'Everything stays private to you.' Nothing is stored and no model sees the contacts, so the claim is overstated rather than false.

confirmed.title: The page tests mock away the globe and skip several required behaviours
confirmed.what: The tests mock NetworkGraph, so the camera turn, focus kept on a pressed chip, the lit count and fullscreen are never exercised. The Find test only asserts 'at least 22'. The banned-words test never renders an answer, an error notice or the Attio form. Nothing tests sort or paging surviving a view change, drag and drop, the reset after Remove all, or the answer limit of 100. This is why page-1, 2, 3 and 8 pass the suite.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 26-33 mock the graph; lines 243 'toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(22)'; lines 344-356 render with ATTIO_ENABLED unset and no answer. No test uses fireEvent.drop or requestFullscreen (grep over tests/unit).
confirmed.fix: Add page tests that use onViewNode with a sort set, the 100-result answer, Remove all with a source turned off, and the banned words with an answer and an Attio error rendered.
confirmed.verifierNote: networkR2.page.test.js:26-33 mock NetworkGraph. Line 243 only checks toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(22). The banned-words test (344-356) renders no answer, no error and no Attio form. No test covers a view change after a sort, the 100-result cap, or a reset after Remove all.

refuted.title: Recency label says "before this export" and the typed answer says "last 12 months" for a different window
refuted.why: SPEC.md:97 asks for this behaviour: the window ends at the newest date, and the label reads "in the 12 months before this export" when that date is more than 60 days old. The engine does not move the window silently: query.js:496-501 builds a note ("Your file's newest connection is from …, so this counts back from then.") and line 698 pushes it into notes. 7 against 6 is the intended result.

refuted.title: The flagship '22 at Stripe' under By role pulls back to the whole globe
refuted.why: Reproduced: VC By role, Stripe share 0.622, so wide. But SPEC section 8 asks for this ('when they are spread over more than about a third of the globe it pulls back to the whole globe and pulses'). Far-side faintness is a separate design weakness (see globe-11), not a spec violation.

refuted.title: People who are not lit drop to about 4 to 12% opacity and lose their names
refuted.why: SPEC section 8 asks that people outside a selection be 'dimmed clearly (more strongly the larger the selection)'. dimLevels gives 0.137 to 0.061, against HEAD's 0.16, a modest change the spec requests. Suppressing names and dimming initials for people who are not lit is unchanged from HEAD (HEAD lines 635, 641). Hover still finds them.

refuted.title: Clicking a group on the globe no longer goes into it; breadcrumb and group rows are lost
refuted.why: SPEC section 2 makes a click on a group a selection, and section 6 hides the group rows while a selection is active. The 'focus root / breadcrumb All' evidence comes from the mocked globe. The real globe turns towards the lit people and then calls reportView, which updates viewId and so the breadcrumb.

missed.title: First read-out sentence names a role group that is everyone
missed.what: The opening sentence takes familyRanked.slice(0,2) (line 263). familyRanked has no upper bound (the 0.9 cap exists only for rolePool at 154), so a single-role file leads with a fact that says nothing.
missed.evidence: 3,000 Software Engineers: "You know 3,000 people at 11 companies: 3,000 engineers." 60-person non-Latin file: "You know 60 people at 4 companies: 60 engineers."
missed.fix: Name a family in the sentence only when its count is under n (same 0.9 cap as the chips), or say "all engineers" once.

missed.title: "Strongest in" sentence has no upper bound and states a sector covering everyone
missed.what: Line 277 requires only strongest[1] >= n*0.1. The industry chip is capped at 0.6 n (line 165), but the sentence is not.
missed.fix: Apply the same <= 0.6 n bound, or drop the sentence when the sector holds everyone.

missed.title: Place sentence says "Most are in" when everyone is there
missed.what: Line 283 says "Most are in X (k)" even when k === n.
missed.evidence: 90 investors all in San Francisco: "Most are in San Francisco (90)." with n=90.
missed.fix: When k === n, say "All are in X." or drop the sentence.

missed.title: Default arrangement is "role" when no arrangement is useful
missed.what: defaultGrouping (line 525) returns 'role' when usefulGroupings is empty. network.js:504 also falls back to 'role'. A file with no titles is then laid out by a facet the page has just said cannot be used.
missed.evidence: Address book of 250 contacts with name and email only: groupings [], defaultGrouping 'role'. The read-out says they "cannot be grouped by employer or role".
missed.fix: Return null (or a flat layout) when no grouping is useful, and have the page show everyone ungrouped.

missed.title: CSV formula guard skips leading-space formulas and mangles negative numbers
missed.what: cell() tests /^[=+\-@\t\r]/ on the raw value. A company of ' =1+1' is written unguarded. A title of '-2' becomes "'-2" (a literal apostrophe in the downloaded file).
missed.fix: Test the value after trimming leading whitespace. Leave a value that is a plain number unguarded.

missed.title: JPMorgan/McKinsey '& Co.' keys keep a dangling 'and', so '& Co.' and '& Company' spellings never merge
missed.what: Suffix stripping removes 'co' and leaves 'and': 'JPMorgan Chase & Co.' gives 'jpmorgan chase and', 'McKinsey & Co.' gives 'mckinsey and', and 'McKinsey & Company' gives 'mckinsey and company'. These are three different keys for spellings that are routinely mixed in one LinkedIn export.
missed.evidence: normalizeCompanyKey('JPMorgan Chase & Co.') gives 'jpmorgan chase and' (reproduced).
missed.fix: After popping the legal suffixes, also pop a trailing 'and'. Treat 'company' as a suffix when it is preceded by 'and'.

missed.title: Background click on the globe no longer clears the selection
missed.what: HEAD had onBackgroundClick={() => setSelected(null)}. Now it is onBackgroundClick={() => setOpenId(null)} (line ~889). After clicking a company or group, clicking empty globe leaves everything dimmed, the 'N lit' badge up and the trail animating. The only way out is the panel's Clear.
missed.evidence: git show HEAD:src/pages/network.js line 1237 against the current network.js onBackgroundClick; pick and selection are untouched by it.
missed.fix: Have onBackgroundClick also call setPick(null) (and, if wanted, clear the chips, Find and the answer), matching HEAD.

missed.title: Canvas aria-label points screen-reader users to a navigator that was removed
missed.what: The aria-label says 'Use the navigator below the map to move through it.' The bottom 'Map navigator' nav (Zoom to / Next layer) existed in HEAD (network.js line 1251) and is gone; the spec moved it into the panel's group rows.
missed.evidence: grep finds no 'Zoom to' or 'navigator' in the current src/pages/network.js; the HEAD version has <nav aria-label="Map navigator">.
missed.fix: Reword it to point at the people panel's list and group rows on the right.

missed.title: Pick selections are not re-filtered to the atlas after a filter change
missed.what: pick.keys are fixed when clicked. Toggling a source chip or 'direct only' rebuilds the atlas, but the pick stays. The panel drops the missing people via byPersonId, while the globe treats them as lit (hasLit true). This leads to globe-14 (rays at alpha 2, names hidden) when none remain, and a badge count lower than the panel title count from the label.
missed.evidence: selection memo: `if (pick) return pick;` has no intersection with visible ids; NetworkGraph hasLit = lit.size at line 541.
missed.fix: Intersect pick.keys with byPersonId in the selection memo (keep the Set stable with useMemo), or clear the pick when visibleContacts changes.

missed.title: With a source turned off, an answer drops visible matches ranked below 100 and inflates the total
missed.what: The question is answered over every contact: the server's saved copy when signed in, or body.contacts = contacts (not visibleContacts) when signed out. The server keeps the top 100, and only then does shownAnswer remove people from hidden sources. If LinkedIn is off and many of the top 100 are LinkedIn contacts, visible matches ranked 101 and below are never shown, while the list says 'Top X of Y' and 'N more hidden by the source filters'. Y is answer.total minus only the hidden people inside the top 100, so it still counts hidden-source matches beyond 100.
missed.evidence: network.js:696-702 sends contacts.map(...), the unfiltered list. network.js:540-561: keep() filters the returned results, and total = Math.max(results.length, answer.total - removed). server query.js:35 sets MAX_RESULTS = 100.
missed.fix: Signed out, send visibleContacts. Signed in, send the active source and direct-only filters to /api/network/query so the server ranks and counts only the people in view.

missed.title: Breadcrumb has no current marker
missed.what: The 'Where you are on the map' nav marks the current level only by font weight. No element in the file has aria-current, so a screen reader cannot tell which crumb is the current place.
missed.evidence: grep -c aria-current src/pages/network.js returns 0. Breadcrumb buttons are at about lines 922-933.
missed.fix: Add aria-current="location" to the last crumb.

missed.title: The 'hidden by filters' count includes 'Possibly related' and intro rows
missed.what: shownAnswer's keep() adds to the same hidden counter for results, intro.direct, intro.possiblyRelated, every viaInvestors group and possiblyRelated.results. The note '{n} more matches are hidden' therefore counts weaker 'possibly related' rows as matches, and can count one person twice when they appear in two sections.
missed.evidence: network.js:540-552: one `hidden` counter is incremented by every keep() call.
missed.fix: Count only results and intro.direct as hidden matches, and de-duplicate by person id.

missed.title: Example question built from a long company name answers nobody, or goes to the model
missed.what: The first-screen example question "Who do I know at {company}?" is built from the company chip without a check that the rules can read it back. cleanEntity (query.js:145) rejects names over six words, so the example shows a count and answers 0 by rules. With the model on, the file's company name is sent to it.
missed.evidence: 30 contacts, 10 at "Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board of Trustees Canada": the example reads "Who do I know at Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board of Trustees Canada?=10". Asking it gives calls=1, parsedBy=llm, total=0 (model mocked).
missed.fix: Have example and company-chip questions call the API with an explicit company filter (like target), not as free text. Alternatively, in parseQuestionRules accept a captured phrase of any length when it equals a company in the file.

missed.title: Signed-out request with no contacts still calls the model
missed.what: The route needs no sign-in and has no rate limit. With no contacts it still runs answerQuestion with useLlm true, so anyone can spend model calls with any question text. The page guards against empty contacts, but the API does not.
missed.evidence: handler({method:'POST', body:{question:'tell me something interesting please'}}) signed out: code=200, chatComplete calls=1, contactCount=0.
missed.fix: Return 400 (or answer with rules only) when the contact list is empty. Allow the model only for signed-in users, with a per-user limit.

missed.title: "Diligence" questions return the whole CRM file
missed.what: Every role found in a CRM or operator file (executive, founder, operator, clinician, professional) carries the diligence lens. So "who can help with diligence" lights everyone and says nothing.
missed.evidence: crm roles {executive:149, founder:29, professional:26, operator:50, clinician:74}. "who can help with diligence" gives total=328 of 328, and "diligence on Stripe" gives 328.
missed.fix: Narrow the diligence lens to expert roles (academic, clinician, consultant, lawyer, accountant, press), or require a company or industry with it. When the lens covers more than about 60% of the file, add a note asking for a company or field.

missed.title: "from X and Y" companies are read as keywords, not companies
missed.what: COMPANY_PATTERNS (line 181) have no "from". "people from Stripe and Google" becomes OR keywords over title, company and tags. Intent is general, so the people-at versus possibly-related split is skipped and anyone whose title mentions Google is counted as if they worked there.
missed.evidence: vc "people from Stripe and Google" gives understood "Mentions stripe; Mentions google", intent general, total 41.
missed.fix: Add `from` to the company patterns when the captured phrase matches a company in the file.

missed.title: The model cannot return tags, industries or dates, so its answer drops them
missed.what: validateFilters (line 506) and LLM_SYSTEM keep only companies, roles, keywords, locations and lens. When the model is used, a question about the file's tags or dates can only come back as keywords, which do not test connectedOn, and "understood" cannot show them.
missed.evidence: query.js:508-515 builds f without tags, industries or connected. scoreContacts reads connected only from filters.connected.
missed.fix: Fix the rules gaps (ask-16, ask-21) so these questions never reach the model, or extend the schema with connected and tags validated against the file's vocab on the server.

value: On all six samples every example question returned exactly its promised count with useLlm false (e.g. Stripe 22, investors 112, clinicians 100, Austin 27).
countIfAdded equals combine().keys.size for every chip pair on all 22 test files; no mismatch found.
VC file leads with 112 investors, 97 engineers, 22 at Stripe, 19 at Google as the spec asks.
Founder file has no investors chip; healthcare leads with 100 clinicians; LP list opens By tag with 'all of them investors or allocators'.
Small file (22) drops the sector and recency sentences; one-person file shows one sentence and no chips, without crashing.
No shortcut shows a count of zero or of everyone on any test file (fits() holds).
Duplicate rows are merged: 100 rows of 25 people give n=25 and matching chip counts.
Future dates (2027, 2030) and unreadable 'yesterday' are kept out of the recent window; mixed slash/word formats parse.
profileNetwork on 3,000 contacts ran in 20 ms; on the 544-person VC file in 5 ms.
Typed tag questions work: 'prospects in New York' 20, 'everyone tagged champion' 57, 'Who is tagged decision maker?' 62.
Role questions typed with chip words match chip counts (founders and CEOs 78, product and design people 75, senior leaders 201).
No banned words (API, key, token, free, paid, tier, quota, Raise, Source, Diligence) in any generated sentence or chip label I saw.
globe: placeClusters at 1, 2, 3, 17, 300 and 1,000 clusters: no pair closer than 0.015 rad, coverage at or under 0.62, largest cluster at [0,0,1].
Placement time: 300 clusters 8 ms, 1,000 clusters 51 ms; 30,000 generated contacts take 15-19 ms to wrap and 85-160 ms to build the atlas.
By company on the 544-person VC sample takes 1 ms to wrap (was 31 s); every node lies on the unit sphere.
Placement is deterministic: same radii give equal output.
spreadOf: one person gives share 0; two people exactly opposite give dir null and home camera; empty input gives zeros.
The pulse does not restart on hover or resize: pulse.current is set only in the highlightIds effect.
The 'N lit' count equals the panel count: both use the atlas built from visibleContacts, and ids not in the atlas are not counted.
Unmount cancels the pending frame and clears the settle timer; the wheel listener is removed; no frames left queued.
Device pixel ratio is capped at 2: a 500x400 canvas at dpr 3 measured 1000x800.
No hex colours, dark: variants or text-[ classes outside THEMES; the badge uses tokens (bg-white and text-ink flip at night).
The opening swing is skipped when intro is false and under reduced motion; later data changes settle in 600 ms.
Not checked without a browser: real raster time, night-theme look, phone layout, pinch on touch hardware, full-screen transition.
ask: Every shortcut and More chip on all six files, asked as its natural question, returns exactly the chip's people, except the old-export recent chip on the small file.
Every example question's card count equals answerQuestion total on all six files.
Only the system prompt and the question text (cut to 500 characters) are sent to the model. No contacts, tags, cities or vocab go into the prompt.
Tag, industry, wordRe and phrase RegExps escape file text. A 500-character pathological question parses in about 1 ms.
At 30,000 contacts with 4,000 distinct tags, each question took 49 to 225 ms with the rules only.
networkLink.js still finds the founders, ceos, ctos, cfos, executives and investors groups with .match. helpers.js still gets results, role and roleLabel.
The route accepts only POST, cuts the question to 500 characters, limits contacts to 30,000 (413), and accepts a 15 MB body. 30,000 contacts are about 7.8 MB.
Text dates (14 Jan 2026, 1/14/2026, January 14, 2026, 14.01.2026, ISO with time) become ISO and survive a second normalisation.
A file with no dates or locations gets a plain note. An old export counts back from its newest date and says so.
"recently" uses the same 12-month window as the recent chip (79 on the VC file).
data: Family assignment on the six samples: every distinct title (about 100) mapped to a sensible family; no chip over 5% wrong by family.
No chip on any sample has count 0 or count equal to N; no two chips on VC or CRM hold the identical set of people.
combine(a,b).keys.size equals countIfAdded(p,[a],b) for every pair of the 12 VC chips.
combine caps at three parts; countIfAdded with three active returns the intersection count.
buildAtlas: companyIndex reaches every person at every company under role, company, industry, place and tag on four samples; no duplicate node ids.
One-bucket first layer is skipped: LP list By role opens on industries, not one 'Investors & LPs' bubble.
Recent window excludes the exact day one year back, includes today, and uses 'before this export' when the newest date is over 60 days old.
Tags are lower-cased, trimmed and de-duplicated across case; '@handle' tags are ignored.

buildAtlas at 30,000 contacts takes 42-200 ms under every arrangement, within the one-second budget.
The throwaway test tests/unit/features/zzReview.data.test.js was deleted; notes are in the scratchpad review-data folder.
page: Remove all no longer calls setExpanded; it deletes, clears the selection and shows a success notice (existing test passes).
LinkedIn, CSV/XLSX, X (connect, import, disconnect) and Attio connectors are all kept, in Connectors.js, opened from 'Add or replace'.
?ask= still runs once when contacts load; drag and drop still works on the empty card and on the source strip.
Full screen still wraps the map section, and the breadcrumb is kept under the globe.
A selection keeps the atlas reference; highlightIds is one Set per selection, and pressing a sort keeps that Set's identity.
Source chips and 'direct only' clear the selection and send the view back to the root; freshData resets the arrangement on upload.
groupBy falls back to profile.defaultGrouping when the chosen arrangement no longer splits the file.
Copy and Download take the whole list beyond 50; Copy shows 'Could not copy' when the clipboard is unavailable.
Shortcut chips are buttons with aria-pressed; the Everyone chip is pressed only with no selection.
No hex colours, dark: variants or arbitrary text sizes in network.js or the new components; NetworkHelpers moved text-[11px] to text-xs.
The interface text in the new page files contains no API, key, token, free, paid, tier, quota, Raise, Source or Diligence.
An error from a question is shown with role=alert under the ask box; notices use role=alert or role=status.
